newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end stronger, outperform on dollar.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end stronger, outperform on dollar.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Thursday, with spreads to U.S. long bonds narrowing amid tame U.S. economic data and an impressive gain in the value of the Canadian dollar, analysts said.

"It started off mainly with the strength of the Canadian dollar," said David Yu, a fixed-income portfolio manager with Perigee Investment Counsel Inc. "All those (U.S.) numbers on the surface weren't bad."
Canada's 30-year benchmark rose C$0.65 to C$110.45 to yield 7.113 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 18/32 to yield 6.91 percent. The spread between the two bonds narrowed to 20 basis points from 21 basis points at the close of trading on Wednesday.

Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets began the session stronger this morning after a U.S. report that showed initial U.S. jobless claims for the week ended April 26 rose more than expected. Another U.S. report showing slightly slower growth in manufacturing during April provided further support.
Canadian bonds outperformed U.S. treasuries amid an impressive rally by the currency.
The dollar rallied past C$1.3900 (US$0.7194) earlier on Thursday amid buying by international funds. The sharp rally in the currency prompted the Bank of Canada to intervene to slow its rise.
Investors are now looking ahead to the release of the key U.S. non-farm payrolls report for April on Friday.

"The technical indicators are still healthy, so it wouldn't surprise me if we can sail through the employment number tomorrow," said Sheldon Dong, manager of fixed-income research with Midland Walwyn Capital Inc.
